n: The division of Canaan west of the Jordan begins. It is led jointly by Eleazar the high priest, Joshua, and the tribal heads — spiritual and civil leaders working together.
The land was assigned by casting lots, as God commanded through Moses. Leaving the choice to God prevented favoritism and quarrels.
Two and a half tribes already had land east of the Jordan; the Levites received no tribal territory.
Joseph’s descendants counted as two tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh, keeping the number of land-receiving tribes at twelve even without Levi. The Levites got towns and pastureland instead.

f.w: the children of Joseph were two tribes

n: Israel divided the land just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

f.w: As the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did

n: Before the lots are drawn, Caleb steps forward. Now an old man, he reminds Joshua of God’s promise to both of them at Kadesh-barnea, when they were the only faithful spies.

f.w: Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite
f.g: A Kenizzite — his clan may have joined Israel from outside and been fully adopted into Judah.

n: At forty, Caleb had scouted the land and given an honest report from his heart.

f.w: as it was in mine heart

n: The other spies terrified the people, but Caleb “wholly followed the Lord” — a phrase repeated three times in this chapter as Caleb’s defining trait.

f.w: I wholly followed the LORD my God

n: Moses swore that the land Caleb had walked on would belong to him and his descendants forever.

f.w: the land whereon thy feet have trodden

n: God kept Caleb alive forty-five years, through the wilderness and the conquest. Now he is eighty-five. (Subtracting the 38 wilderness years suggests the conquest took about seven years.)

f.w: the LORD hath kept me alive, as he said

n: Caleb claims he is as strong as he was at forty — ready for battle. A beautiful picture of lifelong faithfulness and vitality.

f.w: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now
to go out, and to come in
f.g: To lead in battle and daily life.

n: He asks for the hardest territory: the hill country where the giant Anakim lived in big, walled cities — the very place that once frightened Israel. His confidence rests on God’s presence.

f.w: if so be the LORD will be with me

n: Joshua blesses his old companion and gives him Hebron.

f.g: A formal blessing confirming the inheritance.

n: Hebron stayed with Caleb’s family because he wholly followed the Lord. Faithfulness over a lifetime is rewarded.

f.w: because that he wholly followed the LORD God of Israel

n: Hebron’s old name was Kiriath-arba, “city of Arba,” a great Anakite hero. And the land had rest from war — a breather before the division continues.

f.w: the land had rest from war
